subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on moments and the principle of moments, then mark my answer against the spec.
promptWeak: Explain the principle of moments for GCSE Physics simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.

options: The push or pull of a force in a straight line
The energy transferred by a force
The rate at which a force does work
The turning effect of a force about a pivot
questions.explain: A moment is the turning (rotational) effect of a force acting about a pivot. Forces can make an object rotate; the moment measures how strong that turning effect is.

questions.q: Which equation correctly gives the moment of a force?
options: moment = force + distance
moment = mass x acceleration
moment = force x perpendicular distance from pivot
moment = force / distance
questions.explain: Moment (N m) = force (N) x perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force (m). The distance must be measured at right angles to the force.

questions.q: A force of 20 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 0.5 m from a pivot. What is the moment?
options: 40 N m
10 N m
questions.explain: Moment = force x distance = 20 N x 0.5 m = 10 N m.

questions.q: A spanner produces a moment of 30 N m using a force of 60 N. At what perpendicular distance from the bolt is the force applied?
options: 2 m
questions.explain: Rearrange moment = force x distance to distance = moment / force = 30 / 60 = 0.5 m.

questions.q: Why does using a longer spanner make it easier to undo a tight bolt?
options: It increases the mass of the spanner
A greater distance from the pivot gives a larger moment for the same force
It changes the direction of the force needed
It reduces the friction on the bolt
questions.explain: Moment = force x distance. Increasing the distance from the pivot increases the moment produced by the same force, so the turning effect is greater and the bolt turns more easily.

questions.q: According to the principle of moments, an object is balanced (in equilibrium) when:
options: the total anticlockwise moment is greater than the total clockwise moment
the total clockwise moment is greater than the total anticlockwise moment
the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about the pivot
all the forces acting are equal in size
questions.explain: The principle of moments states that when an object is balanced about a pivot, the total clockwise moment equals the total anticlockwise moment about that pivot.

questions.q: On a balanced seesaw, a 4 N weight sits 3 m to the left of the pivot. A weight W sits 2 m to the right. What is W?
options: 2 N
6 N
questions.explain: For balance, anticlockwise moment = clockwise moment. 4 N x 3 m = 12 N m = W x 2 m, so W = 12 / 2 = 6 N.

questions.q: A uniform beam balances on a central pivot. A 10 N force acts 0.4 m from the pivot on one side. On the other side a force acts 0.8 m from the pivot. What force is needed to balance the beam?
options: 8 N
5 N
questions.explain: Balancing moments: 10 N x 0.4 m = 4 N m. The other side: F x 0.8 m = 4 N m, so F = 4 / 0.8 = 5 N.

questions.q: How does a lever such as a crowbar make a job easier?
options: It reduces the total work that must be done
It acts as a force multiplier, giving a larger output force from a smaller input force
It increases the mass being moved
It removes the need for a pivot
questions.explain: A lever acts as a force multiplier. Applying an effort at a large distance from the pivot produces a large moment, giving a bigger output (load) force acting over a shorter distance. Work is not reduced, only the input force.

questions.q: A lever is used to lift a load. The effort is applied 1.2 m from the pivot and the load acts 0.3 m from the pivot. An effort of 50 N is used. What load can just be lifted?
questions.explain: At the point of lifting, effort moment = load moment. 50 N x 1.2 m = 60 N m = load x 0.3 m, so load = 60 / 0.3 = 200 N.

questions.q: In a gear system, a small gear drives a much larger gear. Compared with the small gear, the large gear turns:
options: faster and with a larger moment
at the same speed with the same moment
more slowly but with a larger moment (turning effect)
faster and with a smaller moment
questions.explain: A larger gear has more teeth, so it turns more slowly than the smaller driving gear but transmits a larger moment (greater turning effect). Gears are used to change the size and direction of the turning effect.

questions.q: What happens to the direction of rotation when two gears mesh directly together?
options: Both gears rotate in the same direction
The direction depends only on the gear size
Both gears stop rotating
The meshing gears rotate in opposite directions
questions.explain: When two gears are directly meshed, they rotate in opposite directions. Their teeth interlock, so as one turns clockwise the other must turn anticlockwise.

questions.q: What is meant by the centre of mass of an object?
options: The point where the object is heaviest
The geometric edge of the object
The point where the object touches the ground
The single point at which the whole weight of the object can be considered to act
questions.explain: The centre of mass is the point at which the entire weight of an object can be taken to act. For a uniform, symmetrical object it lies at the centre of symmetry.

questions.q: Which change would make an object more stable (less likely to topple)?
options: Raising its centre of mass and widening its base
Lowering its centre of mass and widening its base
Raising its centre of mass and narrowing its base
Lowering its centre of mass and narrowing its base
questions.explain: An object is more stable when it has a low centre of mass and a wide base. This means it can tilt further before its centre of mass passes outside the base, at which point it would topple.

questions.q: What is the resultant force acting on an object?
options: The weight of the object
The largest single force acting on the object
The force of friction only
The single force that has the same effect as all the forces acting together
questions.explain: The resultant force is the single force that would have the same effect as all the individual forces acting on an object combined.

questions.q: Two forces act on an object along the same line: 12 N to the right and 5 N to the left. What is the resultant force?
options: 7 N to the right
17 N to the right
7 N to the left
60 N to the right
questions.explain: Forces acting in opposite directions along a line are subtracted: 12 N - 5 N = 7 N. The resultant acts in the direction of the larger force, so 7 N to the right.

questions.q: Two forces of 3 N and 4 N act at right angles to each other. Using a scale vector diagram (or Pythagoras), what is the magnitude of the resultant?
options: 7 N
5 N
1 N
questions.explain: For perpendicular forces the resultant is the diagonal: resultant = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = sqrt(9 + 16) = sqrt(25) = 5 N.

questions.q: What does it mean to 'resolve' a single force in a vector diagram?
options: To convert the force into an equal moment
To remove the force from the object
To split one force into two perpendicular components that together have the same effect
To add two forces together to find one resultant
questions.explain: Resolving a force means splitting a single force into two components (usually horizontal and vertical) that act at right angles and together have exactly the same effect as the original force.

questions.q: An object has three forces acting on it: 8 N up, 8 N down, and 6 N to the right. What is the resultant force?
options: 6 N to the right
0 N (balanced)
6 N up
22 N to the right
questions.explain: The 8 N up and 8 N down cancel out (resultant 0 vertically). Only the 6 N to the right remains, so the resultant force is 6 N to the right.
